analysis.one_liner: Eicher Motors makes Royal Enfield motorcycles and, through its VE Commercial Vehicles joint venture with Volvo, medium and heavy commercial vehicles.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended September 2026) results came out on 13 November 2026: consolidated net profit rose 15% YoY to ₹1,573 crore on revenue up roughly 20% to ₹7,422 crore, but this missed the Street's ₹1,626 crore estimate. Royal Enfield posted its highest-ever quarterly sales of 3.77 lakh motorcycles (+15% YoY), yet EBITDA margin slipped to 23.7% from 24.5% a year ago. October 2026 standalone numbers showed the trend continuing: Royal Enfield motorcycle sales +7% YoY, exports +47% YoY, and VECV commercial-vehicle volumes +35% YoY.
analysis.plain_terms: Eicher is selling more motorcycles than ever, but it is making slightly less profit on each one it sells. That's happening because buyers are shifting toward cheaper sub-350cc bikes and electric models, while sales of the pricier above-350cc bikes (where Royal Enfield earns its best margins) actually fell in the first half of this financial year. So the headline 'record sales' number hides a less flattering story underneath: this quarter was volume-led, not margin-led, and margins went the wrong way. The stock is priced for a continuation of the old premium story, which is the tension to watch.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026): net profit ₹1,573 crore (+14.9% YoY from ₹1,369 crore), revenue from operations ₹7,422 crore (+20.3% YoY); one source puts total income growth at +18.9%, a small discrepancy likely from which income lines are included - treat the company's own filing as the reference point if checking further. EBITDA margin fell 0.8 percentage points YoY to 23.7%, even as Royal Enfield volumes hit a record 376,722 units (+15% YoY). Management/commentary attributes this to a mix shift: H1 FY27 saw declining volumes in the above-350cc (premium) segment and growth concentrated in sub-350cc and EV motorcycles, which carry thinner margins. No non-comparable or accounting-reclassification issues were flagged for this quarter.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is only 5.6% below its 26 Feb 2026 peak of ₹8,105 - this is a mild pullback (-5.16% over 3 months, against a Nifty up 3.19%), not a crash. Over 1 year the stock is actually up 12.77% versus the Nifty's -2.84%, so it has beaten the broader market recently. The weaker picture is relative to its direct peer: over 3 years Eicher is up 105.73% against TVS Motor's 171.78%, and over 5 years up 200.18% against TVS Motor's 524.61% - a large and widening performance gap. The only corporate action on record is a 1:10 stock split in August 2020, which is routinely back-adjusted in price history and does not understate returns (unlike a demerger/spin-off); so this gap is a genuine relative-performance story, not a data artefact.
analysis.valuation_read: Eicher trades at roughly 35x trailing earnings and about 8.3x book value, with ROE near 25% and ROCE near 31%. Why it is expensive: the market is paying up for a zero-debt, high-return business with pricing power and genuine export optionality (motorcycle exports up 47% YoY in October). Whether it is cheap: no - at these multiples the stock needs earnings growth to keep accelerating, and this quarter's margin compression plus the miss against analyst estimates (₹1,573 crore versus ₹1,626 crore expected) cuts against that, at least for now.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was volume-led (record 376,722 Royal Enfield units, +15% YoY) rather than margin-led - in fact margins moved backward, with EBITDA margin down to 23.7% from 24.5%. That is a weaker combination for a business whose investment case has historically rested on premiumisation, since volume growth concentrated in cheaper segments is less durable for profitability than growth that comes with margin expansion.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting cleanly into cash: the company carries effectively zero financial debt and sits on net cash of roughly ₹5,564 crore (debt-to-equity near 0.005), alongside a 25% ROE and 31% ROCE. There is no financial risk here. The risk that matters is business risk - specifically whether the current dip in above-350cc volumes and the resulting margin pressure is a temporary mix blip or the start of a more structural slowdown in the premium segment.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding stood at roughly 49.1% as of September 2026 (via the Lal family's Siddhartha/Simran/Tara benefit trusts), with zero shares pledged - a consistent and reassuring signal. FIIs hold about 27.1% and DIIs about 14.9%. Nothing in the available data points to a well-known marquee individual or fund investor on the register beyond standard institutional holders; none is confirmed, so none should be assumed.
strengths: Zero financial debt and net cash of roughly ₹5,564 crore, with ROE near 25% and ROCE near 31%
Record Royal Enfield quarterly volumes of 376,722 units in Q2 FY27, up 15% YoY
Motorcycle exports up 47% YoY in October 2026 (11,915 units vs 8,107 a year earlier), a growing new demand lever
Zero promoter pledging on a stable ~49% promoter holding
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell to 23.7% from 24.5% YoY as above-350cc (premium) motorcycle volumes declined in H1 FY27
Q2 FY27 profit of ₹1,573 crore missed the Street estimate of ₹1,626 crore
Valuation is stretched at roughly 35x P/E and 8.3x P/B, described by some trackers as having moved from 'expensive' to 'very expensive'
Stock has materially underperformed peer TVS Motor over 3 years (105.73% vs 171.78%) and 5 years (200.18% vs 524.61%)
analysis.one_thing: Whether above-350cc (premium) Royal Enfield volumes and the EBITDA margin recover in H2 FY27 - that will settle whether the recent mix shift toward cheaper bikes is temporary or structural, and whether the current ~35x earnings multiple is justified.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 profit, revenue and Royal Enfield volume figures were cross-checked across multiple outlets (Business Standard, Upstox, Samco) and are consistent. Revenue growth is cited as either +20.3% (revenue from operations) or +18.9% (total income) depending on the source - a minor line-item difference, not flagged as a comparability issue by the company. Shareholding percentages, net cash/debt, and P/E-P/B-ROE-ROCE figures come from secondary aggregators (Trendlyne, MarketsMojo, Koalagains, TipRanks) rather than a directly verified exchange filing, and valuation multiples varied slightly (35-36x P/E) across sources - treat as indicative rather than exact. Price, returns, dividend and split data were taken as supplied and not recomputed.
